subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
passage:
Subject: Who depends on my pay

Dear Shalini,

Last week I sat down with a pen and drew a small chart. In the middle, me. Around me, the people who would feel it first if my pay stopped: Papa and Mummy, whose rent and medicines I cover, and my brother, who is still studying.
It shocked me how many arrows pointed at one salary.
So two gaps became clear. One is a plain life policy that pays out if I am gone, so they can stay in the flat. The other is a health policy in my parents' names, separate from my office one.
You mentioned an adviser you trust. Could you share the contact? I want to ask the questions properly before I decide anything.

Anjali

qa.q: Who is still studying in Anjali's chart?
How did Anjali feel on seeing the arrows in the chart?
qa.a: Anjali felt shocked and sobered by how many arrows pointed at one salary, then moved on to acting.

qa.q: What could Anjali do after speaking to the adviser?
qa.a: Anjali could compare the options on a written checklist and take a few days to decide rather than deciding in the call.

qa.q: How might Anjali's parents see the plan?
qa.a: Anjali's parents would probably feel secure knowing the rent and medicines are covered, though they may feel uneasy that the plan exists at all.

grounding: The email shows a person mapping who depends on their income and considering life cover and separate health cover for parents.

subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
passage: 'Reena, since when do you care about insurance?' That's what you asked me, Anjali. Okay, so last Sunday I made a list on the back of an electricity bill. At the top I wrote: who eats if my salary stops? Mummy, obviously, since Papa's pension barely covers the rent. My younger brother, who's in his second year of college. Then I asked, what would hurt them first? If I died, his fees and the loan on the flat would land on Mummy. So that's a term life policy, purely for protection. Then I thought, what if I'm alive but Papa falls ill? My office health plan covers only me. So Papa and Mummy need their own health cover, apart from mine. I'm not buying anything yet. I'm meeting an adviser on Friday with this list, and it feels like I finally know what questions to ask.

qa.q: What did Reena write at the top of the list?
qa.a: Reena wrote: who eats if my salary stops?

qa.q: How does Reena feel about insurance after making the list?
qa.a: Reena feels steadier and more confident, because the list turned a vague worry into clear questions to ask.

qa.q: Which other approach could suit Reena at the Friday meeting, and why?
qa.a: Reena could turn the list into a short checklist of gaps in order of priority, so the meeting stays on the family's needs rather than on products.

qa.q: How might Reena's mother see this plan?
qa.a: Reena's mother might feel relieved and cared for, since the plan asks what would fall on her if Reena's income stopped.

grounding: It shows a young earner mapping who depends on the income and matching term life cover and separate health cover for the parents to those gaps.

subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
passage: I'm Jagdish, and I share a desk wall with Pranav. On Wednesday, after we'd all chipped in for a teammate's father's surgery, Pranav stayed back at lunch with a marker at the small whiteboard. He drew three circles: his parents in Nashik, his sister still studying, himself. Arrows ran from him to each. Under his parents he wrote 'no pension'. I joked that he was planning a party. He laughed, not really. 'If my salary stops, who gets hurt first?' he said, mostly to the board. Then he wrote two lines: 'term cover, for if I'm gone' and 'health cover for Aai-Baba, not just office plan'. He took a photo of the board before wiping it. I don't know what he bought, if anything. He looked calmer, though, than he had all week.

qa.q: What did Pranav write under his parents?
What might Pranav have been worried about while drawing the circles?
qa.a: He seems anxious that his parents and sister would be left without support if his salary stopped, a fear likely stirred by the teammate's father's surgery.

qa.q: What could Pranav do next with the photo of the board?
qa.a: He could take it to a qualified adviser who does not earn from selling policies and ask which cover fits each gap before buying anything.

qa.q: What would change for Pranav's parents if the second line becomes real?
qa.a: They would have their own health cover, so a hospital bill would not depend only on Pranav's office plan or on colleagues chipping in.

grounding: It shows a colleague watching a young earner map who would suffer if the income stopped and note term cover plus separate health cover for the parents.
